question.worked_solution:
Applying the quotient rule, we get

$$
{lim}_{x\to 3}\frac{\sqrt[3]{10x-3}}{{x}^{2}-3}=\frac{{lim}_{x\to 3}(\sqrt[3]{10x-3})}{{lim}_{x\to 3}({x}^{2}-3)}
$$

We calculate the limits of the numerator and denominator, separately.

Applying the root rule in the numerator, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 3}(\sqrt[3]{10x-3}) & =\sqrt[3]{10(3)-3} \\  & =\sqrt[3]{30-3} \\  & =\sqrt[3]{27} \\  & =3\,.\end{aligned}
$$

For the denominator, we have
 

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 3}({x}^{2}-3) & =(3)^{2}-3 \\  & =6\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently,

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 3}\frac{\sqrt[3]{10x-3}}{{x}^{2}-3} & =\frac{3}{6} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\,.\end{aligned}
$$
